headline_marked: [[NASA calls for private space stations]] to succeed ISS by 2030, offering billions in funding
headline: NASA calls for private space stations to succeed ISS by 2030, offering billions in funding
summary: NASA has issued a request to the US commercial space industry for proposals to develop private space stations, aiming for them to take over from the International Space Station as early as 2030.
details: NASA has officially requested proposals from the US commercial space industry to develop private space stations. These stations are intended to succeed the International Space Station (ISS) as early as 2030, ensuring a sustained human presence in low-Earth orbit.

The 360-page "request for proposals" outlines NASA's need for continued research, technology development, crew training, and mission preparation for the Moon and Mars. Industry responses are due by December 8, with NASA planning to select "two or more" contractors by April.

Future phases of the contract are expected to be worth billions, with Phase 1 winners guaranteed at least $100 million. Companies like Axiom Space, Voyager Space, and Vast Space are expected to bid, while SpaceX appears unlikely to participate for now.

A significant provision addresses crewed transportation. NASA is offering to "furnish" transportation for the first four NASA service missions to private stations, easing a major burden on contractors. This includes helping to broker deals with providers like Boeing, which recently received $359 million to support its Starliner spacecraft.

NASA has also assigned explicit prices for missions, estimating a four-seat crew flight at $325 million and a cargo flight at $300 million for 2030. This support aims to facilitate the challenging task of constructing, testing, and flying orbital space stations.
Industry players are reviewing the extensive document. Marshall Smith, CEO of Voyager's Starlab, expressed appreciation for NASA incorporating industry feedback and looks forward to competing.
